docs.title: lasagna results significance
docs.text:
$ lasagna results significance [OPTIONS] RESULTS_PATH

Test every pair of configs at once, correcting for having asked N times.

Running results compare across a grid one pair at a time is the standard way to manufacture a false positive: at alpha=0.05, six configs make fifteen comparisons and roughly a 54% chance that at least one clears the bar by luck alone. Holm-Bonferroni controls the family-wise error rate over the whole set, so what comes out is a claim about the grid rather than about the pair that happened to look best. Each pair is a paired sign-flip test.

Arguments

Argument Required Description RESULTS_PATH yes results.json from a run

Options

Option Type Default Description --metric, -m str ndcg@10 Metric to test. --benchmark str Which benchmark --correction str holm 'holm' (Holm-Bonferroni) or 'none' --alpha float 0.05 Family-wise significance level --all off Include pairs that did not reach significance

docs.title: lasagna results validate
docs.text:
$ lasagna results validate [OPTIONS] BUNDLE_PATH

Check a bundle is well-formed, complete, and internally consistent.

Recomputes the comparability key, the run id and every aggregate from the recorded fields, so a number edited after the run no longer matches its bundle. It detects mistakes and accidental edits, not tampering: the run id is a content hash, not a signature, and anyone who edits a number can recompute it.

Arguments

Argument Required Description BUNDLE_PATH yes run.json bundle to check

Options

Option Type Default Description --strict off Treat integrity warnings as failures

docs.title: lasagna results view
docs.text:
$ lasagna results view [OPTIONS] RESULTS_PATH

Write one HTML page with everything a run measured.

The header names the experiment, its date and versions; then the stage isolation check, and per benchmark the leaderboard, the Holm-corrected significance table with its verdict, every metric per arm, and a per-query diff between two arms with what each retrieved. The page is one file with no external requests, so it opens offline and can be attached anywhere. A bundle is checked as results validate checks it, and one that fails is refused unless --allow-invalid; a results.json is not validated.

Arguments

Argument Required Description RESULTS_PATH yes results.json from a run (or its folder), or a bundle from results bundle

Options

Option Type Default Description --metric, -m str Metric to rank, test and compare queries by (default: ndcg@10 when recorded) --benchmark str Show one benchmark only --diff The two arms the per-query table compares (default: the top two) --output, -o str view.html HTML file to write --open off Open the page in your browser --allow-invalid off Show a bundle results validate rejects, the page marked INVALID

docs.title: lasagna component validate
docs.text:
$ lasagna component validate [OPTIONS] TARGET

Check a component satisfies its stage contract.

Checks what makes a component safe to swap: it returns the declared type, survives empty input, and does not change what it was handed. The last is what makes a comparison attributable: a component that edits its input changes the results of whatever runs after it.

The target is resolved from the working directory, as a sweep resolves it, so the function you name in a sweep is the one checked here. A function decorated with @lasagna.reranker (or another stage decorator) is checked as the component the sweep would run.

Arguments

Argument Required Description TARGET yes What a sweep would name: a registered component (cross_encoder), my_ideas:keyword_overlap (a decorated function), my_pkg.rerankers:MyReranker (a class) or path/to/file.py:name

Option Type Default Description --stage str Component stage: reranker, query_enhancer, chunker, embedder, retriever, document_processor, generator, agentic_pipeline. agentic_pipeline requires a BaseAgenticPipeline class, not a plain function. --profile, -p str speed Profile whose model a registered component is built with (default speed: the 92 MB cross-encoder, not the settings file's 881 MB one)

docs.title: lasagna configure
docs.text:
$ lasagna configure [OPTIONS]

Configure RAG settings.

With --profile, applies a preset; with --reset, drops the session's own settings. Without arguments, lists available profiles.

Options

Option Type Default Description --profile, -p str Apply a profile: speed, standard, balanced, max_quality, or default (the settings file) --session, -s str default Session ID --force off Apply even if the session's stored documents would no longer be searched (they stay where they are until reindexed); the new models must load --reindex off Reindex the session's documents with the new profile, then apply it; if one fails, the session keeps its profile and every document stays searchable --resume-switch off Finish a profile switch with --reindex whose process stopped before it ended (doctor reports one): runs the same switch again --reset off Drop the session's own settings (set by an SDK client, a patch or an import), so its profile's apply as they are; with --profile, switch as well. docs.title: lasagna serve
docs.text:
$ lasagna serve [OPTIONS]

Start the REST API server, with the configurator web page.

While it runs it holds the local store; lasagna status, search, upload and configure go through it, and benchmark run and benchmark experiment use a store of their own.

Options

Option Type Default Description --port int 8000 Port to listen on. --host str 127.0.0.1 Bind address. Default is loopback; --host 0.0.0.0 exposes the API on every interface, and it is UNAUTHENTICATED (see https://github.com/dolev31/lasagna/blob/main/SECURITY.md). --configurator / --no-configurator on Serve the configurator web page at /configurator. --open / --no-open off Open the configurator in a browser once the server starts. --mcp off Also serve the MCP server (SSE) at /mcp/sse, from this process. Milvus Lite admits one process per store, so this is how an agent and the REST API share one. --session, -s str The session for MCP tool calls and REST requests that name none (default: RAG_SESSION_ID, else 'default').

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: This page lists the metrics a run reports and what each one costs. The full definitions give formulas and edge cases. The metrics version is 1.7. It is part of the comparability key, so numbers from a different version never share a leaderboard group.

docs.title: Retrieval metrics
docs.text:
The retrieval track scores each query's ranked list of metric_k distinct documents (10 by default). Every key carries the cutoff, for example ndcg@10. A document whose chunks appear more than once counts once, at its first rank. The definitions agree with trec_eval 9.0.8.

Metric Key What it measures NDCG@k ndcg@10 Rank-weighted gain, normalized by the best possible order. Linear gain, as in BEIR. Precision@k precision@10 The share of the top k that is relevant. Recall@k recall@10 The share of relevant documents found in the top k. F1@k f1@10 The harmonic mean of precision and recall. MRR mrr@10 The reciprocal rank of the first relevant document. MAP map@10 The mean of precision at each relevant rank. Hit rate@k hit_rate@10 Whether any relevant document is in the top k. R-precision r_precision@10 Precision at the number of relevant documents. Complete recall@k complete_recall@10 Whether every relevant document is in the top k.

The ranked list is the retriever's order, or the reranker's when the pipeline reranks. Context reordering is off for this track, because it is a choice about what the generator reads, not a ranking.

docs.title: Answer metrics without a judge
docs.text:
These cost no LLM call.

Metric Key What it measures Exact match exact_match SQuAD v2 string equality after normalization. Token F1 token_f1 Shared tokens, as in SQuAD v2. ROUGE-L rouge_l Longest common subsequence F1. Answer containment contains_answer Whether a reference answer appears in the answer as whole tokens. Abstention rate abstention_rate The share of answers that decline to answer. Answer similarity answer_similarity Cosine similarity to the closest reference answer. Uses all-MiniLM-L6-v2 on CPU by default.

docs.title: Judged metrics
docs.text:
A judge LLM scores these. A judged metric scores only answerable questions. If every judgment fails, the task fails. The score is never recorded as 0.0.

Metric Key What it measures Faithfulness faithfulness Whether the answer is grounded in the retrieved context. Context precision context_precision Precision of the retrieved context against the reference. Context recall context_recall Whether the context holds what the reference needs. Factual correctness factual_correctness Claim-level F1 of the answer against the reference. Noise sensitivity noise_sensitivity The share of the answer's claims that are wrong yet supported by a retrieved context. Lower is better. Opt in. Context relevance context_relevance Relevance of the context to the question, with no reference. Opt in. Citation recall citation_recall The share of sentences that their citations entail (ALCE). Citation precision citation_precision The share of citations that are not irrelevant (ALCE).

The harness asks for faithfulness, context_recall, context_precision and factual_correctness. Set RAG_EVAL_JUDGE_METRICS to a comma-separated list to change the set. noise_sensitivity and context_relevance are opt-in because they cost many judge calls: about 13 per answer for noise sensitivity over five contexts.

Citation metrics are absent, not zero, when the answer cites nothing or no judge is available.

docs.title: Operational metrics
docs.text:
Lower is better for all of these.

Metric Key What it measures Latency latency_ms, avg_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms Wall-clock time of a query, and its distribution. Tokens and calls input_tokens, output_tokens, llm_calls What the system under test spent. The judge's spend is kept apart as eval_*. Cost estimate cost_usd_estimate Present only when the sweep sets prices:. An estimate, from rates that change. Cache counts llm_cache_hits, llm_cache_misses LLM calls served from the response cache. They describe the run and rank nothing.

llm_calls == 0 means no call was seen. For a retrieval-only arm that is the truth.

docs.title: Decorators and registry
docs.text:
Each stage has a decorator with the same name: lasagna.reranker, lasagna.query_enhancer, lasagna.chunker, lasagna.embedder, lasagna.retriever, lasagna.document_processor and lasagna.generator. All take the same arguments and register under the stage they are named for:

import lasagna

@lasagna.reranker                      # name taken from the function
def by_length(query, text): ...

@lasagna.reranker("keyword_overlap")   # explicit name
def keyword_overlap(query, text): ...

lasagna.reranker("by_length_2", by_length)   # a call, not a decorator

Each accepts paper=, claims= and version= keywords, which a run records as the component's provenance. The function each stage expects is listed in write a component.

The registry holds every component, built in or yours. from lasagna.core.registry import registry gives you the shared instance (also lasagna.registry).

docs.title: Results schema
docs.text:
A results bundle is one JSON file that carries a run and its provenance. You make one with lasagna results bundle, and check it with lasagna results validate. The schema is generated from the same constants the bundler uses, so a hub that validates against it cannot require different fields from the ones Lasagna writes.

Print it, or write it to a file:

lasagna results schema
lasagna results schema -o run-schema.json

The bundle schema version is 1.0. Readers accept 1.0 up to, not including, 2.0.

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text: Field Required What it holds schema_version yes The schema version, "1.0". metrics_version yes The metric definitions. Numbers under different values are not comparable. run_id yes A hash of the bundle contents. Validation recomputes it, so an edited number no longer matches. submitter no An object with name and affiliation. experiment yes The environment and run-level facts. See below. configs yes One entry per benchmark and arm. See below. results yes One entry per benchmark and arm with its metrics and per-query scores. integrity yes warnings and blocking, both lists of strings.

docs.title: experiment
docs.text: Field What it holds environment Required: lasagna_version, python and platform. It has no paths, host names or credential names, because bundles are published. components The paper and claimed metrics of each component the run named, keyed by the name the run used. nothing_samples True when only retrieval ran and no task called an LLM. One run is then the whole answer, and SINGLE_RUN is not raised. determinism One of seeded_per_task, seeded_global_concurrent or seeded. Never "reproducible", because LLM judges and GPU kernels defeat that claim.

docs.title: configs
docs.text:
Each entry describes one arm on one benchmark.

Field What it holds name The arm's name. benchmark The benchmark the entry's key covers. comparability_key A hash of held_fixed. Validation recomputes it. held_fixed The configuration held fixed. See below. varied_dimensions What this arm changed: component slots such as reranker, or config flags. Excluded from the key. varied_levels The value each varied dimension took, so the cells of a factorial are distinguishable.

docs.title: held_fixed
docs.text:
These fields feed the comparability key:

metrics_version, benchmark, split, n_samples, sampling_seed, sample_id_digest, corpus_fingerprint, corpus_provenance, resolved_mode, embedder_model, embedder_dim, chunker, retriever_top_k, vector_backend, judge_model, bm25_stemming, fixed_stages, similarity_model and corpus_ingest_gap.

corpus_provenance defaults to native. A field a metrics version did not have yet is not required from older bundles. See comparability and provenance.

docs.title: results
docs.text: Each entry has benchmark_name, config_name and metrics, and usually per_sample_scores: one row per query. A retrieval row carries _retrieved_ids, the ranked list the metrics were computed on, and _retrieved with the document id, score and rank of each result. The rank is authoritative. Scores can tie, so sorting by score does not rebuild the ranking.

docs.title: Integrity messages
docs.text: blocking problems make lasagna results validate fail. warnings do not, unless you pass --strict. The codes you will meet include SINGLE_RUN, UNRESOLVED_JUDGE_ALIAS and PARTIAL_CORPUS. See read and publish results.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text:
Generated by scripts/gen_settings_doc.py from src/lasagna/core/config.py and src/lasagna/settings.lasagna.toml. Do not edit by hand: run the script.

Where a setting comes from, lowest priority first:

  1. the default below;
  2. settings.lasagna.toml, [rag] table (LASAGNA_SETTINGS_FILE names another file);
  3. the environment variable: LASAGNA_<NAME>, or RAG_<NAME> (the older name, still read; LASAGNA_ wins when both are set);
  4. the session (lasagna configure --profile <name> -s <session>, the REST API or MCP).

The settings file and environment variables are the process defaults. A session's profile and overrides are kept in the session database and win over both for that session only.

An environment variable that does not parse, or is outside the allowed values, stops the process with an error naming it, except log_level, which warns and keeps its default: it is also the lasagna command's console level (WARNING unless set), and a typo in it must not stop lasagna doctor. A RAG_ variable that is not a setting is ignored with a warning that suggests the closest one. Booleans take true/false, 1/0, yes/no or on/off; lists and objects take JSON.

Data lives in ~/.lasagna (LASAGNA_DATA_DIR): the databases in dbs/ (LASAGNA_DB_DIR) and uploads in uploads/ (LASAGNA_UPLOAD_DIR). A ~/.rag_knowledge from an earlier version is moved there on first use.

docs.text: The servers, the MCP server and the vector stores read these from the environment only: not from the settings file, and not per session.

docs.title: REST API and authentication
docs.text: Variable Default Description RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH false When true, only a verified X-Session-Token names a session, and POST /api/v1/sessions needs an X-API-Key. When false, binding beyond loopback is refused at startup unless RAG_BIND_IS_PROTECTED is set. RAG_API_KEYS unset Comma-separated keys, each at least 32 characters, that may mint session tokens when RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH is on. Rate limits and quotas are counted per key, over all the sessions it minted. RAG_JWT_SECRET a random secret per process Signs session tokens (HMAC-SHA256). Unset, tokens stop working when the process restarts; with RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH on, an unset, placeholder or shorter-than-32-character secret stops the server at startup. RAG_SESSION_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS 604800 How long a session token is valid, in seconds (7 days). RAG_ADMIN_TOKEN unset The X-Admin-Token for /api/v1/admin/* and for naming a session in POST /api/v1/sessions. Unset, a placeholder or shorter than 32 characters: the admin routes answer 503. RAG_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_SESSION false With RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH on, keep the anonymous default session usable. RAG_BIND_IS_PROTECTED false Says that something outside the process (a loopback port mapping, a NetworkPolicy, a firewall) restricts access, so the server may bind beyond loopback with auth off. RAG_ALLOW_HEADER_IDENTITY false Accept the X-User-ID header as the user identity; otherwise it is refused with 401. RAG_CORS_ORIGINS empty Comma-separated origins allowed cross-origin requests (REST and MCP over HTTP). Empty allows none; * is refused at startup when RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH is on. RAG_ALLOWED_HOSTS unset Extra Host names the REST API and MCP over HTTP answer to with auth off, comma-separated (name, or name:* for any port), such as a container's service name. Otherwise only localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1]. RAG_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS 127.0.0.1 Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted. The image reads gunicorn's FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS first. RAG_MAX_BATCH_FILES 20 Files in one POST /api/v1/documents/batch; more is refused with 400. RAG_MAX_BATCH_BYTES 209715200 Total body of one batch upload (200 MiB); more is refused with 413 before the body is read. RAG_SEARCH_TIMEOUT 120 Seconds a REST search may run before it answers 504. RAG_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_KEY 100 With RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH on, how many sessions one API key may mint per token lifetime (RAG_SESSION_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS); one more answers 429. Raise it for an application that makes a session per end user. RAG_EMBED_MCP false Mount the MCP server at /mcp inside the REST process, for single-process deployments such as Milvus Lite. RAG_CONFIGURATOR false Mount the configurator UI at /configurator, with its API routes. LASAGNA_LOG_FORMAT text json writes one JSON object per log line; text shows a request's id before the message. Any other value stops the server at startup. PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR unset The directory gunicorn workers share for Prometheus metrics (set in the image). RAG_WORKER_METRICS_PORT unset The port a Celery worker serves its Prometheus /metrics on, with RAG_ENABLE_PROMETHEUS on (lasagna_ingests_total for the documents it processed). Unset, the worker serves none. Compose and Kubernetes set 9100.

RAG_SESSION_ID unset The session an MCP tool call, or a REST request without X-Session-ID, uses when it names none (else default). lasagna serve -s sets it. docs.title: Docker and Compose
docs.text:
The deploy folder holds a Docker Compose stack and Kubernetes manifests. The stack runs the REST API, PostgreSQL for metadata, Redis, one vector store, and optionally a Celery worker, an MCP server and Jaeger.

No Docker? lasagna serve runs the same REST API in one process. See REST API.

You need Docker with Compose v2, make, openssl and git.

docs.title: Start the stack
docs.text:
The image builds from a clone of the repository. The pip package does not carry the build context.

git clone https://github.com/dolev31/lasagna.git
cd lasagna/src/lasagna/deploy
cp .env.example .env

# The two required secrets
sed -i.bak "s/^RAG_JWT_SECRET=$/RAG_JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)/" .env
sed -i.bak "s/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)/" .env

make up       # make validate, then docker compose up -d
make health   # GET /api/v1/health, pretty-printed

With .env.example as it ships, this starts Milvus, PostgreSQL, Redis, the API, the Celery worker and beat, and the MCP server. The first make up builds the image, which downloads the embedding and reranker models into it.

Service Address REST API http://127.0.0.1:8000 (interactive docs at /docs) MCP server http://127.0.0.1:8005/sse

Every published port is bound to 127.0.0.1.

make up returns once the containers are created. To return only when every service passes its healthcheck:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f backends/milvus.yml up -d --wait

docs.title: Choose a vector store
docs.text:
VECTOR_BACKEND names a fragment in backends/. .env.example sets it to milvus. To use another store for one command, pass it to make:

make up VECTOR_BACKEND=qdrant

An environment variable (VECTOR_BACKEND=qdrant make up) has no effect while .env sets it, because the Makefile includes .env and that assignment wins. Pass the same value to make down, make logs and make ps.

VECTOR_BACKEND What the fragment adds milvus (default) A Milvus standalone container. milvus-lite No container. Milvus Lite runs in the API process. pgvector No container. The PostgreSQL service switches to the pgvector image. qdrant A Qdrant container. weaviate A Weaviate container. opensearch An OpenSearch container with its security plugin disabled. pinecone No container. Set PINECONE_API_KEY in .env.

The image installs the client libraries for Milvus, Milvus Lite, pgvector and OpenSearch. The qdrant, weaviate and pinecone fragments add the vector-backends extra at build time, so make build builds the right image. After you switch to one of those three, run make build VECTOR_BACKEND=qdrant (or the one you chose). make validate refuses an image built without the client and names the command.

The connection a fragment sets lives under environment:, so a QDRANT_URL in .env does not reach the services. To use a store outside the stack, edit the fragment or write your own.

docs.title: Milvus Lite runs alone
docs.text:
Milvus Lite is a file that one process opens. With VECTOR_BACKEND=milvus-lite, the API runs one worker, serves MCP itself at /mcp/sse on port 8000 and processes uploads in its own threads. The worker, beat and MCP containers could not open the file, so make validate refuses milvus-lite together with the celery or mcp profile. Run it with no profiles:

make up VECTOR_BACKEND=milvus-lite COMPOSE_PROFILES=

docs.title: Choose the services
docs.text:
COMPOSE_PROFILES in .env picks the optional services. .env.example sets it to celery,mcp.

Service Profile What it does api always The REST API, on port 8000. postgres always Metadata: documents, citations, profiles and sessions. redis always Cache, rate-limit buckets and the Celery broker. Not published on the host. celery-worker celery Processes uploaded documents, four at a time. celery-beat celery Schedules the periodic garbage collection and orphan scans. mcp mcp A standalone MCP server over SSE, on port 8005. jaeger tracing Trace UI on port 16686.

Without the mcp profile, no MCP server runs, except with milvus-lite.

docs.title: Turn on auth before you publish the API
docs.text:
The stack starts with RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH=false and publishes the API on 127.0.0.1. In that mode, anything that can reach the port can read and delete any session's documents. To publish the API beyond loopback, set these in .env and restart:

cat >> .env <<EOF
API_BIND=0.0.0.0
RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH=true
RAG_API_KEYS=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
EOF
make up

A client then asks for a session token with one of the keys. See Authentication. The deployment README lists what else auth changes. SECURITY.md says what authentication does and does not protect.

docs.title: CPU or GPU image
docs.text:
The image runs the CPU-only build of torch. For a host with an NVIDIA GPU, build with the CUDA build instead:

make build TORCH_VARIANT=cuda

make up reuses an image that exists, so switching variants needs make build. The API, worker and MCP containers also need GPU access: the NVIDIA Container Toolkit on the host, and a gpus: all entry on those services.

docs.title: Make targets
docs.text: Target What it does make up Run make validate, then start the stack. make validate Check the config. It stops when a required secret is empty, the backend name is wrong, or the profiles conflict with milvus-lite. make down Stop the stack and keep the volumes. make down-v Stop the stack and delete its volumes: documents, metadata and uploads. make build Rebuild the image. make logs Follow every log. make logs SVC=celery-worker follows one. make ps List the containers. make health Call GET /api/v1/health on the API port. make shell Open bash in the API container. make test Check the files and the merged compose config. It starts no container. make help List the targets.

docs.title: Healthchecks
docs.text:
Service Check api GET /api/v1/health/ready, with 300 seconds to load the models on a cold start. mcp GET /health on port 8005. redis, postgres redis-cli ping and pg_isready. milvus, qdrant, weaviate, opensearch The store's own health endpoint.

The API, worker, beat and MCP services start after Redis and PostgreSQL are healthy.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text: The k8s/ folder holds a Kustomize base and one overlay per vector store. overlays/local.example is the template for the overlay that holds your secrets. See the deployment README for the manifests.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text: The MCP server gives an agent search over your documents. It works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and any other MCP client. It serves 29 tools for search, documents, configuration and document lifecycle. By default a client sees 22 of them.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
A client that launches the server itself (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor) runs it over stdio, which is the default:

lasagna-mcp

To serve several clients from one process, start it on a port:

lasagna-mcp --transport sse --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8005

--host and --port apply only to --transport sse. Passing them without it is an error.

Mode Use it for Command stdio (default) A client that launches the server lasagna-mcp SSE Several clients, or a server behind a proxy lasagna-mcp --transport sse --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8005 Embedded One process for REST and MCP lasagna serve --mcp -s <session>, served at /mcp/sse

With the embedded mode, -s names the session that calls use when they name none. RAG_EMBED_MCP=true has the same effect as --mcp.

One process at a time for a local store

A local Milvus Lite store opens in one process at a time. While lasagna serve runs, a lasagna-mcp call answers at once with the server's /mcp/sse endpoint. Start the server with --mcp and register that URL in the client.

docs.title: Connect a client
docs.text:
Add this to claude_desktop_config.json. Claude Code reads the same block from .mcp.json in your project.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lasagna": {
      "command": "lasagna-mcp",
      "env": { "RAG_SESSION_ID": "my-corpus" }
    }
  }
}

RAG_SESSION_ID is the session a tool call uses when it names none. The agent then searches the documents you uploaded with lasagna upload FILE -s my-corpus. If lasagna-mcp is not on the client's PATH, give its absolute path inside your virtual environment.

To register a running server by URL instead:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lasagna": { "type": "sse", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/sse" }
  }
}

From Python:

import asyncio
from lasagna.sdk.integrations import MCPKnowledgeClient


async def main():
    async with MCPKnowledgeClient("http://localhost:8005/sse") as client:
        result = await client.search("What is RAG?", session_id="demo")
        print(result)


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Choose a tool set
docs.text:
Set Select it with What it serves safe (default) --tools safe or LASAGNA_MCP_TOOLS=safe 22 tools. Every tool except the seven below. all --tools all or LASAGNA_MCP_TOOLS=all All 29 tools.

The seven tools that only all serves delete data, reset configuration or change the server-wide retention policy: delete_document, clear_session, bulk_delete_session, rebuild_collection, delete_rag_profile, reset_rag_config and set_lifecycle_policy.

Under safe, these seven are not registered. No client can call them, and the docs page cannot either. To serve them from a client config, add "args": ["--tools", "all"] next to "command".

patch_rag_config stays in safe. It changes only the caller's session, and you can patch the change back. A change that would leave stored documents unsearchable is refused unless you pass force=true.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Tools that work on data take an optional session_id, which scopes documents and configuration. Without it, a tool acts on the server's session. Multi-user setups also pass session_token. No tool requires session_id.

Group Count Tools Search 2 search, get_document_context Documents 6 upload_document, list_documents, get_document_info, get_document_chunks, get_document_status, delete_document (all only) Lifecycle 6 archive_document, restore_document, get_gc_status, get_lifecycle_policy, bulk_delete_session (all only), set_lifecycle_policy (all only) Session 3 set_focused_documents, get_focused_documents, clear_session (all only) Config 9 get_rag_config, patch_rag_config, list_profiles, get_active_profile, set_active_profile, save_rag_profile, get_profile_stats, reset_rag_config (all only), delete_rag_profile (all only) System 3 get_system_status, reindex_document, rebuild_collection (all only)

Use search to retrieve. It runs the session's retrieval pipeline and returns context with inline citations and a <search_metadata> JSON block. With no LLM configured, a session set to agentic retrieval runs its standard pipeline, and the metadata's degraded_stages names agentic.

The full description of every tool is in the MCP README. Tool names, descriptions and input schemas follow the deprecation policy in the governance document.

docs.title: Settings that apply to a call
docs.text:
The first source that defines a value wins:

  1. Tool arguments, such as top_k or use_hyde, for one call.
  2. The session: set_active_profile and patch_rag_config (or lasagna configure -s SESSION). These persist across restarts.
  3. The environment: LASAGNA_<NAME> or RAG_<NAME>.
  4. The settings file: the packaged settings.lasagna.toml, or --config-file.

Configuration explains the same order for every surface.

docs.title: Keep it safe
docs.text:
Binding to 0.0.0.0 publishes the tool surface

Without RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH=true, any client that reaches the port can call every tool in the served set. The server refuses a non-loopback bind unless auth is on, or RAG_BIND_IS_PROTECTED=true says something else protects it. With auth on, tools need a session_token from POST /api/v1/sessions. Put a reverse proxy in front for TLS. The default bind is 127.0.0.1.

The docs page at /docs has a "try it" button. It runs on an unauthenticated POST /api/call that can invoke any tool, including deletion. It is off unless you pass --enable-docs-api, and the server refuses to start if you combine that flag with a non-local --host.

SSE mode also serves / (a welcome page), /docs, /health and /sse.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: lasagna serve runs an HTTP server with 41 endpoints: 32 under /api/v1/ and 9 that are not versioned. Every endpoint takes and returns JSON, except the two upload routes, which take multipart form data.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
lasagna serve

The server listens on 127.0.0.1:8000. That address is reachable only from your machine, and it needs no login. Useful options:

Option Meaning --port Port to listen on. --host Address to bind. A non-loopback address needs auth on. --configurator / --no-configurator Serve the settings UI at /configurator. --open Open the browser. --mcp Also serve the MCP server at /mcp/sse. --session, -s The session for requests that name none.

A running server serves interactive docs at /docs and the schema at /openapi.json. When this page and that schema disagree, the schema is right. The /docs page loads its scripts from cdn.jsdelivr.net, so it needs a network connection.

docs.title: Upload and search
docs.text:
lasagna upload report.pdf -s my-corpus

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/search \
  -H "X-Session-ID: my-corpus" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "What does the report conclude?", "top_k": 5}'

Uploads are indexed in the background by default. The upload response comes back with status set to processing. Poll GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/status until it reads ready.

A document id works as an idempotency key. Uploading again with an id the session already owns replaces that document. Without an id, a file whose bytes the session already holds is not uploaded again, and the response names the original in duplicate_of.

The search body has these fields:

Field Default Meaning query (required) The question, 1 to 10,000 characters. top_k 5 Results to return, 1 to 100. min_score none Drop results scoring below this. document_ids none Search only these documents. use_hyde true Use HyDE query expansion. use_reranking true Rerank with a cross-encoder. routing_tier none Force fast, standard or comprehensive.

A stage that failed and fell back is named in degraded_stages, so an empty list means every configured stage ran.

docs.title: Endpoints at a glance
docs.text:
Group Routes Health GET /api/v1/health/live, /health/ready, /health, and GET /api/v1/stats Sessions POST /api/v1/sessions Documents POST /api/v1/documents, POST /documents/batch, GET /documents, and GET, DELETE, /chunks, /status, /reindex, /archive, /restore under /documents/{document_id} Admin Garbage collection, orphan repair, the lifecycle policy and session deletion under /api/v1/admin/ Search POST /api/v1/search, /search/citations, /search/multi-query, /search/agentic Citations GET /api/v1/citations and /citations/{citation_id} Config GET and PATCH /api/v1/config, GET /config/profiles, PUT /config/profiles/{profile_name} Pipelines GET /api/v1/pipelines Configurator Eight routes under /api/config/knowledge Reindex POST /api/knowledge/reindex

The endpoint reference documents each route with its request, response and status codes.

docs.title: Sessions and identity
docs.text:
A session scopes documents and configuration. The server reads the session from the first of these that is present:

  1. X-Session-Token header (a signed token).
  2. X-Session-ID header.
  3. session_id query parameter.
  4. The name default.

A session id is at most 128 characters. A token that is present but invalid or expired is refused with 401. It does not fall through to the next source.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Out of the box, auth is off, and the server binds only to loopback. Turn auth on before you expose the server to anyone else:

export RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH=true
export RAG_JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export RAG_API_KEYS="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
lasagna serve --host 0.0.0.0

With RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH=true:

  • Only a verified X-Session-Token names a session. A bare X-Session-ID is refused with 401, and so is the default fallback, unless RAG_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_SESSION=true.
  • POST /api/v1/sessions mints tokens and needs an X-API-Key header with a key from RAG_API_KEYS. Keys are at least 32 characters.
  • Tokens are signed with RAG_JWT_SECRET and last 7 days by default (RAG_SESSION_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS). An unset or placeholder secret is a startup error. Without auth, an unset secret gets a random one per process, so tokens stop working on restart.
  • The health probes stay open.

Instance-wide admin routes need an X-Admin-Token header that matches RAG_ADMIN_TOKEN. If that variable is unset, they answer 503.

With auth off, the server refuses to start on a non-loopback address unless RAG_BIND_IS_PROTECTED=true says that something outside the process restricts access. A request with a non-loopback Host header gets 421 unless the host is in RAG_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Set RAG_CORS_ORIGINS to allow browser clients.

These security variables are read under their RAG_ names only.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Limit Default Setting One uploaded file 50 MiB RAG_MAX_FILE_SIZE One batch upload 200 MiB and 20 files RAG_MAX_BATCH_BYTES, RAG_MAX_BATCH_FILES Other request bodies 1 MiB fixed One search 120 seconds RAG_SEARCH_TIMEOUT Concurrent uploads 5 RAG_MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS Sessions per API key 100 RAG_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_KEY Request rate 60 per minute, burst 10, adaptive RAG_RATE_LIMITING_ENABLED

Rate limiting is off in the code and on in the Docker and Kubernetes configurations. Each session also has quotas: 1,000 documents, 5 GiB, 100,000 chunks, 600 searches per minute and 200 uploads per hour.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 400 Invalid input: a bad file type, a session id over 128 characters, a malformed query. 401 Missing, invalid or expired credentials. 403 You named an identity without a valid admin token. 404 The document, citation or profile does not exist in this session. 409 A conflict: a restore after the grace window, or an embedding size that does not fit the collection. 410 The source file is gone, so the document cannot be reindexed. 413 The file, batch or body is over its limit. 422 The body failed validation, or a config key is unknown. 429 Rate limited or over quota. Rate limits include Retry-After. 500 An unhandled backend error. 503 The backend is starting, a dependency is down, the processing pool is full, or the embedding model is not downloaded. 504 The search ran past RAG_SEARCH_TIMEOUT.

A server never downloads a model inside a request. If the session's embedding model is not on disk, search answers 503 with the command that fixes it.
